user_reviews.Name: Kay
user_reviews.Description:
Very small restaurant on the main road.
the shop had around 4 tables and when we went, there was only 1 person working (we think) and so, service was really slow. They would being us 1 of our mains, then 10 minutes later the next one, then another 10 minutes later the final one - even if 2 of them were the exact same dish. We didnt understand why it would takr that ling in between to being the next dish when the 2 dishes were the same. We only ordered cooked food but it was also the same for the raw dishes.

we ordered the beef bowl and 2 of the special curries (chicken + prawn).

1. beef bowl: ok. normal. beef on top felt like its been out in the open for a short while as it was starting to dry out. taste wise it was good - simple but comforting.
2. curries: the amount of curry varied between the 2 mains. rice was decent portion. The prawsns  were crispy on the outside and juicy inside - and fried extremely straight so I'm not sure if they were homemade or store bought.

After the lady finishes bringing food out to everyone in the restaurant,  she finally served us all some tea/water - by that time we had already finished our meal due to the slow service.

Overall it was ok but nothing special or super memorable.

user_reviews.Description:
Ohana opened about three months ago.
It is a small Japanese restaurant situates in Sales but  gives you a surprise of signatures  Japanese cuisines.
The impressive bright, tidy and clean dinning hall can accomondate almost 20 guests. A reservation is a  must and expected.
As we know the chef is a young Hong Konger at his late 30s. People told me the chef hadn't any experience worked in a Japanese restaurant. His cooking skill is learnt by his talent and instinct that it makes he  known to gourmets. One cannot deny, like some youths,  the chef should be so fervent in Japanese culture. Likewise, he could  make out the so wonderful Japanes foods.
Why not have an assorted sashimi as recommended by  a lady service  staff.
It makes us have a brilliant light of pleasent surprise when the assorted sashimi was put before us. The sashimi - salomon, tuna, scallop and  sweet shrimp were so delicious, fresh and tender that we have never had in Manchester.  They instantly melt in our mouth when swallowing.
The Tonkotsu Sauce Ramen is one of it in the menu. The ramen noodles were chewy and firm, not mushy. Two pieces of the Japanes - style BBQ pork could have a thumb up.
The assorted sashimi rice bowl is the one you never forget! The rice had a very generous portion to fill your stomach.
Deep fried oysters were the  ones taken into our order.  Wrapped by a layer of coating power filled with an oyster, it needs a skill not to overdo  the fresh oyster remarkably with juice tast. The chef could make it.
The appetites were the seaweed salad and a hot miso soup to wake up your tast buds. Terrific！
I had a chance to challenge the chef that I wish to have a bite of "Salted Grilled Ox Tongue" when I come again some date.
Ohana is a Japanese restaurant to be recommended.

user_reviews.Name: Nikki C
user_reviews.Description:
It was okay for what it was. Did the job! We were going to the Fury V Hall boxing match at AO. Perfect location, literally over the road. With road closures for every event from previous experience, it was so easy to just go across the road on foot.
Jonathan on reception was very helpful after I called asking for a quiet room as it is positioned on the main ring road. Perfect room request of 419- lovely view over green quarter at the back of the hotel and super quiet. No road noise at all.
Parking at AO discounted from £26 to £13 for 24hr by popping your reg in the tablet at the check in desk. Amazing price for city centre. Don’t be put off if the carpark says fully booked online- they only sell 200 odd spaces out of 900 for pre booking. You won’t get the discounted rate in pre book.
Nice enough rooms too. Hotel communal areas and dining area lovely decor.

Now for the cons. Bathroom wasn’t the cleanest. Dirty grout in shower. Remote for tv was filthy and no complimentary water in the fridge? Usually standard. Especially at £200PN on event night.
If you’re a light sleeper bring an eye mask as the smoke detector in the room flashes green every couple of minutes.
Pillows incredibly flat even with 2 so maybe ask reception for more?

Breakfast was okay. Hot and cold options, plenty of drinks but no hash browns was a disappointment. They don’t do them. Also 10 mins before breakfast ends the host was going around all the tables telling them breakfast was over. Continued doing this and more frequently a couple mins past breakfast time. I get they have a closing time but at a 4star hotel you don’t expect to be chased like that.

Anyway, brill for location but not worth £200. I’d probably say £80 on a normal night would be about right.

Jonathan on reception was very helpful after I called asking for a quiet room as it is positioned on the main ring road. Perfect room request of 419- lovely view over green quarter at the back of the hotel and super quiet. No road noise at all.
Parking at AO discounted from £26 to £13 for 24hr by popping your reg in the tablet at the check in desk. Amazing price for city centre. Don’t be put off if the carpark says fully booked online- they only sell 200 odd spaces out of 900 for pre booking. You won’t get the discounted rate in pre book.
Nice enough rooms too. Hotel communal areas and dining area lovely decor.

Now for the cons. Bathroom wasn’t the cleanest. Dirty grout in shower. Remote for tv was filthy and no complimentary water in the fridge? Usually standard. Especially at £200PN on event night.
If you’re a light sleeper bring an eye mask as the smoke detector in the room flashes green every couple of minutes.
Pillows incredibly flat even with 2 so maybe ask reception for more?

Breakfast was okay. Hot and cold options, plenty of drinks but no hash browns was a disappointment. They don’t do them. Also 10 mins before breakfast ends the host was going around all the tables telling them breakfast was over. Continued doing this and more frequently a couple mins past breakfast time. I get they have a closing time but at a 4star hotel you don’t expect to be chased like that.

Anyway, brill for location but not worth £200. I’d probably say £80 on a normal night would be about right.

night out knowing the staff genuinely care about their guests.

user_reviews.Name: Jullian Agostinho
user_reviews.Description:
I’ve been coming to Pho Cue since early 2022. I used to go at least twice a month, so I feel like I can give a fair and honest review.

The food has consistently been one of the reasons I keep coming back. It’s still my favourite Vietnamese restaurant in Manchester. The original team was fantastic, especially the lady who used to welcome people at the door who no longer works there. She always made everyone feel looked after and was very agile handling big queues etc. There’s also another member of the original team who’s still there, and she’s always so friendly and welcoming. I genuinely enjoy it when she’s looking after my table.

A special mention also goes to Jason. I first met him when he was a waiter, and he always remembered me and my friends whenever we came back. That personal touch really makes a difference, and honestly, knowing Jason is still there is one of the reasons I continue to return.

That said, I also want to mention something that has disappointed me over the past couple of years. The gentleman who manages the queue has never been particularly welcoming. I completely understand the restaurant gets very busy. That’s not the issue. It’s more that this has become a pattern over several visits. He often comes across as though he’s doing customers a favour rather than welcoming them into the restaurant. Customer service is just as important as the food, and I think this is an area that could be improved.

As for the food, where do I start? The Vietnamese coffee is incredible. The pork spring rolls are an absolute must, and honestly, any of the salt and pepper or garlic butter dishes are excellent. If you’re not sure what to order, try the lamb chops or the beef with fried rice instead of jasmine rice (missing pics but I promise it’s worth it). You can thank me later. The BBQ duck is another favourite if you enjoy rich, saucy flavours, and the Special Pho is absolutely amazing.

Overall, I still think Pho Cue is well worth visiting. The food has kept me coming back for over four years, and that’s not something I say lightly. I just hope the front-of-house experience becomes as consistently good as the kitchen.

One final suggestion. Maybe consider closing at 10pm instead. 😅

Pho delivers a solid 4-star experience if you’re craving something warm, comforting, and full of flavor. The pho broth is rich and aromatic without being too heavy, and the portions are satisfying. Their menu has a good range of Vietnamese classics, so it’s easy to find something whether you’re in the mood for noodles, rice dishes, or lighter bites.

The atmosphere is casual and lively, making it a great spot for a quick meal or a relaxed catch-up with friends. Service is generally efficient and friendly, even during busy times.

user_reviews.Description:
Whenever i come up to Manchester & stay in Northenden, I always visit @vietguymanchester for their fabulous and amazing authentic food and warm hospitality 😍😋👏🙌
I can certainly recommend the following dishes, which i had on this trip:
Papaya salad with prawns beautiful fresh papaya, mango, carrot, vegetables & prawns in a fresh dressing, I'm not lying when I say i could eat this every day for breakfast ❤️😋😋😋😋😋😋

You really must come and give them a try, you won't be disappointed, but be mindful they are popular, so if travelling I recommend you book 👍👌
Love these guys 👏👏🙌🙌🙌

user_reviews.Name: Hoàng
user_reviews.Description:
As an international student, finding a place that truly reminds me of home is priceless—and this restaurant does exactly that! The food here is absolutely authentic and full of flavor. I tried several dishes, and each one was amazing:
• The beef curry with turmeric rice was rich, creamy, and perfectly seasoned. The beef was tender, and the rice had a wonderful aroma with crispy shallots on top.
• The stir-fried noodles with chicken and vegetables were fresh and well-balanced, with just the right amount of crunch and seasoning.
• And of course, the pho was outstanding! The broth was clear yet packed with depth, the beef slices were fresh, and the herbs added that classic Vietnamese touch.
The portions are generous, the presentation is beautiful, and the atmosphere is cozy—perfect for anyone craving a taste of Vietnam. I highly recommend this place to anyone who loves authentic Vietnamese cuisine or wants to experience it for the first time. Definitely coming back!

The chicken was tender, juicy and packed with fragrant lemongrass flavour while the salad was crisp, tangy and easily my favourite part of the meal. user_reviews.Description:
Doux Chaton is an interesting spot. I only discovered it in Manchester by chance while walking past. I’d been to the Liverpool branch before and had mixed feelings, mostly because the service wasn’t great - the owner (middle aged woman not the elder lady, she’s lovely) there didn’t seem very accommodating, which left me a bit unsure about trying it again.

The Manchester branch was a better experience. We were welcomed by one of the female managers, who was super kind and friendly, so we felt like giving it a proper try. Another time, we were served by a friendly guy, but he seemed a bit lost and the ordering process wasn’t as smooth as we hoped.

The interior looks nice, very cafe-like and casual, which I liked. My only real shocker was the prices. A small bowl is £14.50 and a large is around £17. That’s pretty steep compared to places like Pho Cue, I Am Pho, or Ca Phe Viet, which are around £12 for a large. Plus, there’s a 12.5% service charge added and you have to pay upfront rather than after eating, feels quite extortionate and you’d never get this at any other Vietnamese restaurant in Manchester.

The pho itself is decent, but I still prefer the other spots I mentioned as they have more depth of flavor. I’ve tried a few other dishes here too, like the banh mi, which was a miss for me because the Maggi sauce overpowered the toppings. I also tried the Vietnamese coffee, both the salted and egg versions, and was let down, they came out bitter without the sweet notes you’d expect from Vietnam.

Overall, it’s an okay cafe to sit in and the service can be great at times, but I’d say the prices and some of the dishes don’t quite justify a repeat visit.
